newsitem.title: USA: US attache-- new high for Australia wheat exports.
newsitem.headline: US attache-- new high for Australia wheat exports.

text.p: A U.S. agricultural attache predicted Australia wheat exports would reach a new high, saying three-quarters of the record 1996-97 export crop already sold.

In a report dated April 2 and released in Washington on Monday, the attache said most of Australia's 23.5 million tonne crop had now been harvested and delivered to the Australian Wheat Board and "the aim is to export up to 20 million tonnes."
Attache reports are not official USDA data.
The attache said the wheat board had sold close to 15 million tonnes of wheat to overseas markets by the end of March, the halfway mark of the marketing year.

The attache said another record result was that 8.5 million tonnes of the wheat has already been shipped since October and a further 2.5 million tonnes were expected to be shipped in April. He said sales and shipments are running 50 percent ahead of previous highs.
In its latest World Supply and Demand report on March 11, the U.S. Agriculture Department pegged 1996/97 Australian wheat exports at 17.0 million tonnes.

The attache said the Australian Wheat Board had been "pushing hard" to sell the harvest as early as possible to avoid likely pressure on prices later in the year when northern hemisphere crops come onto world markets.
